sections.text: Introduction

This document outlines the hot gas path 
inspection procedure P2, which must be performed for hot gas path inspection 
every 48000 operation hours as indicated by H48000 in the above title block.

The first draft initiated by eng. Ayman El-Mor & 
eng. Ali Mohamed Fahmy at Port Said Gas 
Tutbine, 
tested by eng. Abd El-Hamid Abu Zaid 
at 02 March 2003 , revised by EDEPCo. Inspection 
and Quality control eng. Abouda El-Bana, , 
accepted and approved by Port-Said plant general director eng. El-Aaraby Ali 
Said.
Safety Precautions

items:
A work permit must be issued and the qualified 
maintenance stuff should be carry the suitable safety category

Safety fence (rope) with caution marks 
surrounding the work area is required

Wear your safety helmet, safety shoes
 . etc
Unit must be out of service.
Fire fighting system should be isolated.
Fuel system should be isolated.
Oil system should be isolated.
All switches in motor control center panel should be isolated.
Generator must be fully isolated.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out
DISASSEMBLY
Turbine alignment check

items:
Remove the upper half of the load coupling guard at the load 
 gear and at bearing NO. 2.
Remove the generator coupling covers to allow the turbine rotation.
Remove the coupling guard from the accessory coupling.

Take run outs reading at the forward and aft. Ends of the load coupling and 
 accessory gear shafts.
Record the run outs reading on appropriate sheets.
Remove the load coupling and accessory coupling.

Mount the alignment fixture and take 
 alignment reading on the turbine to load gear and accessory gear to the

items: Combustion chamber accessories and pipes removal
Remove the atomizing airlines from the fuel nozzle.
Remove the fuel lines from the fuel nozzle.
Disconnect the spark plug leads.
Disconnect the flame detector.

Unlock and remove all fuel nozzles take in

sections.text:
Combustion 
Liners Removal

items: Mark each cover with the relative chamber number.
Unbolt and remove the combustion covers.
Remove the combustion liner no 1 as described below:
Remove the crossfire tube clamps from chamber No 1.
Remove the crossfire tube clamps from adjacent chamber N0 2 and No 1.
Push the crossfire tube into adjacent chambers No 2 & No 10.
Remove the liner No 1.
Remove the crossfire tube with the adjacent chamber NO. 2 & NO. 10.
Repeat steps (a) to (e) to remove other liners.

items:

sections.text: Turbine Internal Inspection

items:
Inspect the transition pieces with strong beam of light and records should be 
 made of any visible cracks, deposits or erosion and record the results in the 
 attached record sheet

Inspect the first and second stage nozzle for cracks, distortion, blocked 
 cooling holes, loss of metal and corrosion. Repair is mandatory for nozzles 
 exceed the following limits:

sections.text: Cracks:
Sidewall:

items: Five cracks per nozzle segment 0.5 inch deep and spaced less than 1.0 inch.
Vane trailing edge:

any number of cracks parallel to sidewall and less than 1.0 inch provided 
 that distance between any adjacent cracks is greater than the longer of the 
 two cracks.

Two converging cracks less than 1.0 inch with a part distance less than the 
 total sum of the two cracks.

Two diverging cracks less than 1.0 inch and the length of the crack is less 
 than the distance between the between the end of crack and sidewall.

Vane leading edge: two cracks less than .375 inch and a part distance less 
 than 1.0 inch.

sections.text: Corrosion / Erosion:

items:
bowing of the trailing edge in excess of 0.035 inch with no more than one 
 incident per segment.
No other partition shall be bowed.

Record the inspection results and record the results in the attached record 
 sheet

sections.text: Buckets Inspection

items:
Inspect the first & second stages buckets for cracks, torn metal, dents & 
 erosion of loading and trailing edges.

Compare the inspection results with the manufacture limits and change if 
 necessary.

sections.text: First Stage Bucket Removal

items: Cut out the heads of lock twist pins by sharp chisel

Bush the bucket in the direction of removed head pay attention to the axial & 
 radial seal pins.

Clean out the bucket groove and remove any proud metal caused by cutting 
 chisel or securing peen marks.

sections.text: Exhaust Hood Disassembly

items:
Remove the flex plats from the aft end of the 
 exhaust plenum.
Remove the flex plats from the upper forward half of the plenum.
Remove the feed and drain line to bearing NO.2.

Remove the exhaust turning vanes (diffuser) from the exhaust plenum slide the 
 back against the load gear.

Enter the exhaust plenum and remove the horizontal joint bolting insulation 
 shields then complete the removal of horizontal joint bolts of the inner and 
 outer flanges of the exhaust hood

Break the exhaust hood halves by using jack screws (holes are provided in the 
 outer flange for this purpose) lift the exhaust hood vertically (using 2 ton 
 trolley hoist) until it clear the air baffle which is trapped between the seal 
 of bearing NO2 and the hood.
Lift the hood into the stack and then bush it against the load gear direction.

sections.text: Second stage Bucket Removal

items:
Cut out the heads of lock twist pins of the second stage bucket by sharp 
 chisel.

Push the buckets toward the removed pins head gradually as group pay attention 
 to bucket shield slots.

Clean out the bucket groove and remove any proud metal caused by cutting 
 chisel or securing peen marks.

sections.text: Bearing No. 2 Disassembly

items: Remove the upper half of the bearing housing.
Record the clearance of journal bearing & oil seal with rotor.

Remove the upper half of journal bearing liner and take reading of the lower 
 half clearance to the rotor with feeler.
Lift the turbine rotor and roll lower half.

sections.text: Bearing No.2 Inspection

items: Inspect the bearing housing and casing joints for leaks, warping and gouge.
Inspect oil seal packing teeth for oil, dirt, wear and broken seals.
Check air groove for cogging.
Check for indication of shaft/ seal rubbing.

Inspect bearing liner thoroughly for bad scratch, loose Babbitt and high 
 spots.

Check the inside diameter of bearing liner at centers and at inch from 
 either side at the horizontal joint.

Record the bearing liner diameters reading and to be compared against the data 
 shown on drawings in attached sheet

Change the bearing if the inspection show scratches, high 
 spots, excessive wear out of tolerances.

sections.text:
Bearing 
No. 2 Re-assembly

items:
Clean the bearing liners using kerosene and 
 clean rags. Dont use rags, which may leave lint deposits on the bearing 
 surface. Besides avoid contacting of hard objects to the bearing surfaces.

Apply a thin film of turbine oil to the lower 
 half of bearing liner & role it out to its place while the turbine rotor is 
 still lifted.

Release the hoist lifting the rotor and take 
 reading of shaft / liner clearances at four points (front / rear / right / 
 left).

Compare the clearances with 
 the drawings recommended tolerance to avoid
 tilting or twisting 
 of bearing liners, to achieve
 the recommended clearances 
 flow these steps:

Put 2 mm sheet of asbestos on the 
 upper half of the rotor.

Lift the rotor with 8-ton hoist just 
 to release the liner lower half.

Put the bearing liners upper half to 
 its position and tight both halves with liners bolts.

Release the rotor-lifting hoist 
 &remove the liner upper half.

Check the clearances 
 and record the results in the attached sheet

Measure the total clearance of bearing liner 
 putting 1 mm tin wire on the shaft then re-assemble the upper half of bearing 
 liner and measure the thickness of the tin wire at bearing forward & aft 
 direction.

Re-assemble the liners upper half and bolt 
 the liner.

Re-assemble the seal and record the clearances 
 in attached sheet

Re-assemble the upper half of journal bearing 
 housing and bolt it.
Check the GIB keys of bearing NO 2 housing.

sections.text:
Bearing No. 1 
Disassembly

items: Remove the L-shaped air intake duct.
Remove the upper half skin of the inlet plenum.

Remove the upper half of compressor forward casing. Using two guide bolts is 
 recommended to avoid hitting of the compressor blades.

Remove the upper half of the inlet casing three Allen-head bolts are located 
 in the passage on each side of this casing must be removed.
Remove the upper half of bearing housing.

Measure bearing and seal clearances and record the results in the attached 
 sheet

sections.text:
Bearing 
No. 1 Inspection

items: Check the loaded thrust bearing pads thickness .
Apply axial force in the aft direction to measure forward bearing clearances.

Check the unloaded thrust bearing land taper and compare the taper 
 measures with the drawing limits if the measured taper falls outside the 
 tolerances the bearing must be replaced.

Inspect Babbitt surface of journal & thrust bearing for cracks, chips, 
 scratches, wiping and high spots and record the results in the attached sheet.
No cracks are allowable.

Scratches that less than 0.001 to 0.005 inch deep and less 
 than one inch long can be repaired by scraping down any raised metal and 
 lightly blending out the babbit surface with 0000 steel wool.

Excessive temperature should be not exceeding 5 percent of the 
 lower liner half area.

Check the inside minor diameter of the journal bearing liner at vertical 
 center and the major diameter inch from either side of the horizontal joint 
 and compare these reading with the allowable limits.

Inspect oil seals and packing teeth for oil, dirt, uneven wear, and broken 
 seals take in consideration that bearing NO1 is most critical, since oil 
 leakage could cause compressor fouling & possible loss of output.

sections.text: Bearing No. 1 Re-assembly
Clean the bearing liners using kerosene and clean rags.

Rollout the lower half of the liner and adjust the bearing to shaft clearance 
(right, left, front, rear) to avoid liner tilting or twisting.
Measure the total vertical clearance of bearing liner using 1mm tin wire.
Assemble the upper liner half and bolt the two halves.

Assemble the seals lower halves and record 
their clearances.

Assemble the loaded and unloaded thrust 
bearing and record their clearances.

Clean the bearing housing thoroughly and 
assembly the bearing housing covers and bolts it.

Disassembly

Remove the upper half of the compressor discharge casing hence the inner barrel 
upper half must be freed from the discharge casing - remove the three Allen 
bolts located slightly forward from the junction of the bulked head struts.

Use 4 guide bolts when lifting compressor discharge casing when removing the 
horizontal joint bound bolts they should be driven upwards a step in the lower 
casing prevent them from being driven down.
Remove the upper half of the compressor casing.

Inspect the compressor rotor and stator blades for deposit, erosion or corrosion 
pitting.

Clean the inlet guide vanes thoroughly and perform a liquid penetrate test 
especially to the braze area between the blade itself and the inner shroud ring 
and to the blade root area at the dovetail.

Clean the compressor blading by using organic 
chemical against.

Roll out the bottom rows of compressor fixed blades with the rotor in place. In 
those stages with individual blades there may be spacing shims between some 
blades. These should be carefully marked and replaced in their original position 
at re-assembly.

sections.text:
Inspection of First & 
Second Stage Shrouds

Check the turbine shrouds for clearance with buckets forward; middle, and aft 
end of blade tip record the amount and location of all rubbing on field 
clearance report.
Check for build up on the shrouds (remove by grinding).

Check the first stage turbine wheel to the stator position by using one marked 
first stage turbine bucket. Take four-point feeler gage check and replace the 
upper half of turbine shell.

Change the shroud segments if the radial clearance between bucket tip and the 
shroud exceed the upper limits.

Arrange the shroud segments accordance to the knocked numbers in the shroud 
metal.
Load shrouds in the flow direction and mark the dowel pin hole by drilling.

Remove the shroud segments and drill the 
dowel pinholes on power full machine.

Re-assemble the shroud segments and their 
dowel pin.

Check the bucket tip and the shroud radial clearance and record the results in the 
attached sheet

sections.text: Second Stage Bucket Re-assembly
Arrange the bucket in accordance to the balance sheet.

Place the lock twist pins in their slots and assemble each bucket with 
its seal pins. (Anti size compound is recommended to use for pines)

Push the first bucket into the rotor grove (2cm) and then install the 
next bucket, push the tow buckets into their grove (0.5 cm) and assemble the 
third bucket, push the buckets gradually paying attention to the seal pins.

Rotate the lock twist such that it secure the bucket from moving axial, 
then punch the lock twist with the two diametrically opposite peen marks with 
around nosed punch.

items: Arrange the bucket in accordance to the balance sheet.

sections.text: Exhaust Hood Re-assembly

items:
Lower the upper half of the exhaust hood and tight the horizontal joint bolts 
 of inner and outer flanges be sure that new gaskets are used on the horizontal 
 joint of the inner gas path cone & the air baffle is properly located in the 
 groove of the seal of bearing NO 2 before lowering the hood.

Assemble the horizontal joint bolting 
 insulation shield.

Assemble the exhaust turning vanes (diffuser)

sections.text:
First & Second Nozzle 
Re-assembly

items:
Clean thoroughly the turbine shell and 
 discharge casing

Coat the seal-second stage nozzle spring seal 
 with anti seize

Roll in the second-stage nozzle when in 
 position and supported on the lifting rig insert and bolt the support shims

Lower the second stage nozzle lower half onto 
 the supporting lugs and inserts the bottom eccentric pin.

Assemble the two lower axial holding pins at 
 45.

Assemble the lower half inter stage packing 
 (labyrinth) and spring adjusts the clearances as recommended by the 
 manufacture drawing.

Roll in the lower half of the first stage 
 nozzle and while the nozzle is still supported on the lifting hoist insert the 
 horizontal supporting lugs and bolt tightly and then lower the nozzle.

Assemble the first stage nozzle bottom 
 eccentric pin.

Tighten the first nozzle bottom holding clamp 
 and check their clearance.

Take a complete set of turbine clearance and record the results in the attached 
 sheet
 ** Note that the clearances on the 
 packing and the second stage nozzle must be taken while the nozzle must be 
 waged against the second stage shrouds (this is its running position).

Assemble the upper half of the supporting 
 ring.

Assemble the upper half of the first stage 
 nozzle.

Assemble the upper half of second stage nozzle 
 diaphragm.

Assemble the upper half of second stage 
 nozzle.

Assemble the clamps to the first stage nozzle 
 horizontal joint and check the clearance of the lug U clamp record this 
 clearance on the attached sheet
Assemble the second nozzle clamps and record the results in the attached sheet.

Assemble the two packing strips into the outer 
 seal groove of the first stage nozzle; verify that the lap of the strips is 
 not in line to minimize the possibility of leakage.

Assemble the transition pieces. Starting from 
 the chamber No 5 and work upper wards from that point be sure that the 
 transition pieces are fully engage in the first stage nozzle before tightening 
 the center holding bolts.

Assemble the side seals (L seals) and locking 
 bolt washer combination between each transition pieces.

sections.text:
Shell Casing 
Re-assembly

items: Check thoroughly turbine shell cleaning.

Coat the mating surfaces of the turbine shell hood and discharge casing with a 
 light film of anti-seize.

Check that all is secure within the shell area before assemble, rotate the 
 turbine rotor with ratchet mechanism check if there were any abnormal sound.

Assemble the shells upper half using 4 guide rods and the two jack bolts 
 mechanism pay attention to the turbine shell level during lowering with jack 
 bolts.
Tighten the shell bolts according to the bolting sequence.

Assemble the first and second stage nozzle upper eccentric pins; second stage 
 axial holding bolts at 45 and the bore scope plugs.

Assemble the outer combustion casing using new gasket on the casings and fix 
 them in the groove with grease in two spots.
Remove all support jacks from the unit.
Remove all support jacking located under the turbine.

Power stations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document outlines the hot gas path 
inspection procedure P2, which must be performed for hot gas path inspection 
every 48000 operation hours as indicated by H48000 in the above title block.
The first draft initiated by eng. Ayman El-Mor & 
eng. Ali Mohamed Fahmy at Port Said Gas 
Tutbine, 
tested by eng. Abd El-Hamid Abu Zaid 
at 02 March 2003 , revised by EDEPCo. Inspection 
and Quality control eng. Abouda El-Bana, , 
accepted and approved by Port-Said plant general director eng. El-Aaraby Ali 
Said.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and the qualified 
maintenance stuff should be carry the suitable safety category
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks 
surrounding the work area is required
Wear your safety helmet, safety shoes
 . etc
Unit must be out of service.
Fire fighting system should be isolated.
Fuel system should be isolated.
Oil system should be isolated.
All switches in motor control center panel should be isolated.
Generator must be fully isolated.
Tools and Equipment
Two wrenches set size 3/8″ 
 to 1 1/2″
Two sockets set drive 3/4″ size 3/8″ up to 
 1 1/2″
Two Allen wrench size 3/32″to 1″
Four impact socket wrench drive 1″ size 1 
 1/8″, 1 5/16″, 1 ″, 1 11/16″, 1 7/8″ &2 ″.
Power hand drill, Misc. grinding machine.
Four chain hoists 1 1//2 tons.
Chain hoists 5 tons, Chain hoists 8 tons, 
 and Chain hoists 10 tons.
Eye bolts & shackles.
0.0015 to 0.040 inch feelers.
0 1 inch micrometer.
1 10 inch outside micrometer.
2 12 inch inside micrometer.
Work to be Carried Out
DISASSEMBLY
Turbine alignment check
Remove the upper half of the load coupling guard at the load 
 gear and at bearing NO. 2.
Remove the generator coupling covers to allow the turbine rotation.
Remove the coupling guard from the accessory coupling.
Take run outs reading at the forward and aft. Ends of the load coupling and 
 accessory gear shafts.
Record the run outs reading on appropriate sheets.
Remove the load coupling and accessory coupling.
Mount the alignment fixture and take 
 alignment reading on the turbine to load gear and accessory gear to the 
 turbine and record the results in the attached sheet
Combustion Component and Piping Disassembly
Combustion chamber accessories and pipes removal
Remove the atomizing airlines from the fuel nozzle.
Remove the fuel lines from the fuel nozzle.
Disconnect the spark plug leads.
Disconnect the flame detector.
Unlock and remove all fuel nozzles take in 
 consideration to mark the nozzles with its proper Chamber number.
Combustion 
Liners Removal
Mark each cover with the relative chamber number.
Unbolt and remove the combustion covers.
Remove the combustion liner no 1 as described below:
Remove the crossfire tube clamps from chamber No 1.
Remove the crossfire tube clamps from adjacent chamber N0 2 and No 1.
Push the crossfire tube into adjacent chambers No 2 & No 10.
Remove the liner No 1.
Remove the crossfire tube with the adjacent chamber NO. 2 & NO. 10.
Repeat steps (a) to (e) to remove other liners.
Combustion 
Component 
Inspection
Inspect the crossfire tubes & retainers for 
 (wear, cracks& overheating) and
 record the results in the attached sheet
Inspect and maintain the fuel nozzle according 
 to the appropriate procedure and record the results in the attached sheet
Inspect the cap and liner if 
 it should be reused, repaired or scraped according to the criteria and record 
 the results in the attached sheet
Inspect the transition pieces with strong beam 
 of light and records should be made of any visible cracks, deposits or erosion 
 and record the results in the attached record sheet.
Turbine Compartment 
Accessories Removal
Remove the turbine 
 compartment roof with the diesel engine exhaust manifold & CO2 fire fighting 
 piping connected to this compartment
Remove the turbine 
 compartment stand beams adjacent to the turbine shell
Prepare four lifting lugs on 
 the chimney wall above the center lines of the first stage nozzle, the 
 second stage nozzle, right and left side of the shell
Install three support screw jacks below:
 = 
 Discharge compressor 
 forward to after casing flange 
 = Discharge casing to turbine shell flange 
 = Turbine shell to exhaust hood
Remove atomizing air & gas 
 manifold and fuel oil lines.
Remove cooling air pipes as necessary for 
 removal of the shell
Remove the two second-stage nozzle axial 
 holding bolts located at 45 & borescope plugs from the upper shell half
Remove the wheel space thermocouples & 
 junction boxes adjacent to turbine shell.
Remove the vertical bolting between the 
 turbine shell and compressor discharge shell
Remove the vertical Allen head bolts between 
 the turbine shell and the exhaust hood
Remove the turbine shell horizontal bolting
Jack the turbine shell at the jack bolts holes 
 provided to lift the shell case (it is preferable to use four guides during 
 the shell lifting).
Lift the shell casing using mobile crane, 
 lifting wires and hoists as described in the weight and center of gravity 
 drawing
Remove the eccentric pins for positioning the 
 1st & 2nd nozzles upper halves after removing the upper 
 shell case
Turbine Internals Disassembly
Check and record the clearances 
 of the 1st & 2nd nozzle holding clamps (attachment # 3).
Remove the upper portion of the 2nd 
 stage nozzle holding clamps and the horizontal joint bolting and lift the 
 upper half of the 2nd stage.
Remove the Allen-head horizontal 
 joint bolts from the inner diaphragm upper half and lift it
Remove the combustion outer 
 casing except the combustors No 1, 10, 9
Remove the transition pieces by 
 removing the bolts with the first stage nozzle and side L seal
Push these transition pieces 
 clear of nozzle into the outer combustion chambers.
Remove the first stage nozzle 
 clamp and the horizontal joint bolting
Lift off the upper half of the 
 first stage nozzle careful attention should be paid to the L-shaped seals 
 between the segments
Remove the upper half of 
 supporting ring.
Take 
 a complete set of turbine clearance 
 and record the results in the 
 attached sheet
Remove the first and second stage 
 nozzle lower centering pins & second stage axial holding bolts located at 45 
 & bore scope plugs from the lower shell half.
Untight the seal ring bolts from 
 the first stage nozzle inner support ring and the two axial nozzle clamps.
Remove the first stage nozzle 
 support lugs.
Roll out the first stage nozzle 
 by hooking the tow nozzle sides to two-hoist chain hooked on the lifting lug 
 above the first stage nozzle Transvaal axel with the nozzle swinging 
 free.
Raise one hoist cable and lowering the other side 
 until the nozzle brought out above the turbine shaft, and then lift the stage 
 up.
Remove the second stage nozzle 
 diaphragm lower half packing by bushing it out of its groove.
Tight a rope with wooden blocks 
 of dimension 7*7*12 cm with distance between block of 20 cm around the turbine 
 shaft at the labyrinth packing groove.
Remove the lower half second 
 stage nozzle supporting lugs then remove it by rolling out using tow chain 
 hoist hooked on the lifting lugs above the stage axel the lower half of the 
 nozzle and diaphragm must be lifted as one piece.
Turbine Internal Inspection
Inspect the transition pieces with strong beam of light and records should be 
 made of any visible cracks, deposits or erosion and record the results in the 
 attached record sheet
Inspect the first and second stage nozzle for cracks, distortion, blocked 
 cooling holes, loss of metal and corrosion. Repair is mandatory for nozzles 
 exceed the following limits:
Cracks:
Sidewall:
Five cracks per nozzle segment 0.5 inch deep and spaced less than 1.0 inch.
Vane trailing edge:
any number of cracks parallel to sidewall and less than 1.0 inch provided 
 that distance between any adjacent cracks is greater than the longer of the 
 two cracks.
Two converging cracks less than 1.0 inch with a part distance less than the 
 total sum of the two cracks.
Two diverging cracks less than 1.0 inch and the length of the crack is less 
 than the distance between the between the end of crack and sidewall.
Vane leading edge: two cracks less than .375 inch and a part distance less 
 than 1.0 inch.
Corrosion / Erosion:
bowing of the trailing edge in excess of 0.035 inch with no more than one 
 incident per segment.
No other partition shall be bowed.
Record the inspection results and record the results in the attached record 
 sheet
Buckets Inspection
Inspect the first & second stages buckets for cracks, torn metal, dents & 
 erosion of loading and trailing edges.
Compare the inspection results with the manufacture limits and change if 
 necessary.
First Stage Bucket Removal
Cut out the heads of lock twist pins by sharp chisel
Bush the bucket in the direction of removed head pay attention to the axial & 
 radial seal pins.
Clean out the bucket groove and remove any proud metal caused by cutting 
 chisel or securing peen marks.
Exhaust Hood Disassembly
Remove the flex plats from the aft end of the 
 exhaust plenum.
Remove the flex plats from the upper forward half of the plenum.
Remove the feed and drain line to bearing NO.2.
Remove the exhaust turning vanes (diffuser) from the exhaust plenum slide the 
 back against the load gear.
Enter the exhaust plenum and remove the horizontal joint bolting insulation 
 shields then complete the removal of horizontal joint bolts of the inner and 
 outer flanges of the exhaust hood
Break the exhaust hood halves by using jack screws (holes are provided in the 
 outer flange for this purpose) lift the exhaust hood vertically (using 2 ton 
 trolley hoist) until it clear the air baffle which is trapped between the seal 
 of bearing NO2 and the hood.
Lift the hood into the stack and then bush it against the load gear direction.
Second stage Bucket Removal
Cut out the heads of lock twist pins of the second stage bucket by sharp 
 chisel.
Push the buckets toward the removed pins head gradually as group pay attention 
 to bucket shield slots.
Clean out the bucket groove and remove any proud metal caused by cutting 
 chisel or securing peen marks.
Bearing No. 2 Disassembly
Remove the upper half of the bearing housing.
Record the clearance of journal bearing & oil seal with rotor.
Remove the upper half of journal bearing liner and take reading of the lower 
 half clearance to the rotor with feeler.
Lift the turbine rotor and roll lower half.
Bearing No.2 Inspection
Inspect the bearing housing and casing joints for leaks, warping and gouge.
Inspect oil seal packing teeth for oil, dirt, wear and broken seals.
Check air groove for cogging.
Check for indication of shaft/ seal rubbing.
Inspect bearing liner thoroughly for bad scratch, loose Babbitt and high 
 spots.
Check the inside diameter of bearing liner at centers and at inch from 
 either side at the horizontal joint.
Record the bearing liner diameters reading and to be compared against the data 
 shown on drawings in attached sheet
Change the bearing if the inspection show scratches, high 
 spots, excessive wear out of tolerances.
Bearing 
No. 2 Re-assembly
Clean the bearing liners using kerosene and 
 clean rags. Dont use rags, which may leave lint deposits on the bearing 
 surface. Besides avoid contacting of hard objects to the bearing surfaces.
Apply a thin film of turbine oil to the lower 
 half of bearing liner & role it out to its place while the turbine rotor is 
 still lifted.
Release the hoist lifting the rotor and take 
 reading of shaft / liner clearances at four points (front / rear / right / 
 left).
Compare the clearances with 
 the drawings recommended tolerance to avoid
 tilting or twisting 
 of bearing liners, to achieve
 the recommended clearances 
 flow these steps:
Put 2 mm sheet of asbestos on the 
 upper half of the rotor.
Lift the rotor with 8-ton hoist just 
 to release the liner lower half.
Put the bearing liners upper half to 
 its position and tight both halves with liners bolts.
Release the rotor-lifting hoist 
 &remove the liner upper half.
Check the clearances 
 and record the results in the attached sheet
Measure the total clearance of bearing liner 
 putting 1 mm tin wire on the shaft then re-assemble the upper half of bearing 
 liner and measure the thickness of the tin wire at bearing forward & aft 
 direction.
Re-assemble the liners upper half and bolt 
 the liner.
Re-assemble the seal and record the clearances 
 in attached sheet
Re-assemble the upper half of journal bearing 
 housing and bolt it.
Check the GIB keys of bearing NO 2 housing.
Bearing No. 1 
Disassembly
Remove the L-shaped air intake duct.
Remove the upper half skin of the inlet plenum.
Remove the upper half of compressor forward casing. Using two guide bolts is 
 recommended to avoid hitting of the compressor blades.
Remove the upper half of the inlet casing three Allen-head bolts are located 
 in the passage on each side of this casing must be removed.
Remove the upper half of bearing housing.
Measure bearing and seal clearances and record the results in the attached 
 sheet
Bearing 
No. 1 Inspection
Check the loaded thrust bearing pads thickness .
Apply axial force in the aft direction to measure forward bearing clearances.
Check the unloaded thrust bearing land taper and compare the taper 
 measures with the drawing limits if the measured taper falls outside the 
 tolerances the bearing must be replaced.
Inspect Babbitt surface of journal & thrust bearing for cracks, chips, 
 scratches, wiping and high spots and record the results in the attached sheet.
No cracks are allowable.
Scratches that less than 0.001 to 0.005 inch deep and less 
 than one inch long can be repaired by scraping down any raised metal and 
 lightly blending out the babbit surface with 0000 steel wool.
Excessive temperature should be not exceeding 5 percent of the 
 lower liner half area.
Check the inside minor diameter of the journal bearing liner at vertical 
 center and the major diameter inch from either side of the horizontal joint 
 and compare these reading with the allowable limits.
Inspect oil seals and packing teeth for oil, dirt, uneven wear, and broken 
 seals take in consideration that bearing NO1 is most critical, since oil 
 leakage could cause compressor fouling & possible loss of output.
Bearing No. 1 Re-assembly
Clean the bearing liners using kerosene and clean rags.
Rollout the lower half of the liner and adjust the bearing to shaft clearance 
(right, left, front, rear) to avoid liner tilting or twisting.
Measure the total vertical clearance of bearing liner using 1mm tin wire.
Assemble the upper liner half and bolt the two halves.
Assemble the seals lower halves and record 
their clearances.
Assemble the loaded and unloaded thrust 
bearing and record their clearances.
Clean the bearing housing thoroughly and 
assembly the bearing housing covers and bolts it.
Clean the bearing liners using kerosene and clean rags.
Rollout the lower half of the liner and adjust the bearing to shaft clearance 
(right, left, front, rear) to avoid liner tilting or twisting.
Measure the total vertical clearance of bearing liner using 1mm tin wire.
Assemble the upper liner half and bolt the two halves.
Assemble the seals lower halves and record 
their clearances.
Assemble the loaded and unloaded thrust 
bearing and record their clearances.
Clean the bearing housing thoroughly and 
assembly the bearing housing covers and bolts it.
Compressor Casing 
Disassembly
Remove the upper half of the compressor discharge casing hence the inner barrel 
upper half must be freed from the discharge casing - remove the three Allen 
bolts located slightly forward from the junction of the bulked head struts.
Use 4 guide bolts when lifting compressor discharge casing when removing the 
horizontal joint bound bolts they should be driven upwards a step in the lower 
casing prevent them from being driven down.
Remove the upper half of the compressor casing.
Inspect the compressor rotor and stator blades for deposit, erosion or corrosion 
pitting.
Clean the inlet guide vanes thoroughly and perform a liquid penetrate test 
especially to the braze area between the blade itself and the inner shroud ring 
and to the blade root area at the dovetail.
Clean the compressor blading by using organic 
chemical against.
Roll out the bottom rows of compressor fixed blades with the rotor in place. In 
those stages with individual blades there may be spacing shims between some 
blades. These should be carefully marked and replaced in their original position 
at re-assembly.
Remove the upper half of the compressor discharge casing hence the inner barrel 
upper half must be freed from the discharge casing - remove the three Allen 
bolts located slightly forward from the junction of the bulked head struts.
Use 4 guide bolts when lifting compressor discharge casing when removing the 
horizontal joint bound bolts they should be driven upwards a step in the lower 
casing prevent them from being driven down.
Remove the upper half of the compressor casing.
Inspect the compressor rotor and stator blades for deposit, erosion or corrosion 
pitting.
Clean the inlet guide vanes thoroughly and perform a liquid penetrate test 
especially to the braze area between the blade itself and the inner shroud ring 
and to the blade root area at the dovetail.
Clean the compressor blading by using organic 
chemical against.
Roll out the bottom rows of compressor fixed blades with the rotor in place. In 
those stages with individual blades there may be spacing shims between some 
blades. These should be carefully marked and replaced in their original position 
at re-assembly.
Compressor Inspection
Inspect the compressor rotor and stator blades 
for deposit, erosion or corrosion pitting.
Inspect the external side of compressor casing to be sure there are no cracks.
Check for cracks in the blade root and dovetail by using liquid penetrate test.
Inspect the compressor rotor and stator blades 
for deposit, erosion or corrosion pitting.
Inspect the external side of compressor casing to be sure there are no cracks.
Check for cracks in the blade root and dovetail by using liquid penetrate test.
Compressor Casing Re-assembly
Before re-assembly the lower half casing should be thoroughly clean and free of 
all cleaning residue.
Reassemble the loose blades of the compressor stator lower stages.
Pay attention to the position of the blade in relation to the casing.
Reassemble the upper half of inlet casing. Dont overlook the six Allen-head 
bolts located in the inner barrel directly in the air stream.
Record all compressor clearances in attachment record sheet
Cheek visually the compressor to verify That 
no foreign object or debris is teft in the turbine remember the three axial 
angular bolts holding the inner barrel to the compressor discharge casing Re 
Assemble the discharge casing of compressor
Assemble the compressor after casing
Assemble the compressor forward casing
Re assembles the inlet plenum upper half skin.
Assemble the L shaped air intake duct.
Before re-assembly the lower half casing should be thoroughly clean and free of 
all cleaning residue.
Reassemble the loose blades of the compressor stator lower stages.
Pay attention to the position of the blade in relation to the casing.
Reassemble the upper half of inlet casing. Dont overlook the six Allen-head 
bolts located in the inner barrel directly in the air stream.
Record all compressor clearances in attachment record sheet
Cheek visually the compressor to verify That 
no foreign object or debris is teft in the turbine remember the three axial 
angular bolts holding the inner barrel to the compressor discharge casing Re 
Assemble the discharge casing of compressor
Assemble the compressor after casing
Assemble the compressor forward casing
Re assembles the inlet plenum upper half skin.
Assemble the L shaped air intake duct.
Inspection of First & 
Second Stage Shrouds
Check the turbine shrouds for clearance with buckets forward; middle, and aft 
end of blade tip record the amount and location of all rubbing on field 
clearance report.
Check for build up on the shrouds (remove by grinding).
Check the first stage turbine wheel to the stator position by using one marked 
first stage turbine bucket. Take four-point feeler gage check and replace the 
upper half of turbine shell.
Change the shroud segments if the radial clearance between bucket tip and the 
shroud exceed the upper limits.
Arrange the shroud segments accordance to the knocked numbers in the shroud 
metal.
Load shrouds in the flow direction and mark the dowel pin hole by drilling.
Remove the shroud segments and drill the 
dowel pinholes on power full machine.
Re-assemble the shroud segments and their 
dowel pin.
Check the bucket tip and the shroud radial clearance and record the results in the 
attached sheet
Check the turbine shrouds for clearance with buckets forward; middle, and aft 
end of blade tip record the amount and location of all rubbing on field 
clearance report.
Check for build up on the shrouds (remove by grinding).
Check the first stage turbine wheel to the stator position by using one marked 
first stage turbine bucket. Take four-point feeler gage check and replace the 
upper half of turbine shell.
Change the shroud segments if the radial clearance between bucket tip and the 
shroud exceed the upper limits.
Arrange the shroud segments accordance to the knocked numbers in the shroud 
metal.
Load shrouds in the flow direction and mark the dowel pin hole by drilling.
Remove the shroud segments and drill the 
dowel pinholes on power full machine.
Re-assemble the shroud segments and their 
dowel pin.
Check the bucket tip and the shroud radial clearance and record the results in the 
attached sheet
Second Stage Bucket Re-assembly
Arrange the bucket in accordance to the balance sheet.
Place the lock twist pins in their slots and assemble each bucket with 
its seal pins. (Anti size compound is recommended to use for pines)
Push the first bucket into the rotor grove (2cm) and then install the 
next bucket, push the tow buckets into their grove (0.5 cm) and assemble the 
third bucket, push the buckets gradually paying attention to the seal pins.
Rotate the lock twist such that it secure the bucket from moving axial, 
then punch the lock twist with the two diametrically opposite peen marks with 
around nosed punch.
Arrange the bucket in accordance to the balance sheet.
Place the lock twist pins in their slots and assemble each bucket with 
its seal pins. (Anti size compound is recommended to use for pines)
Push the first bucket into the rotor grove (2cm) and then install the 
next bucket, push the tow buckets into their grove (0.5 cm) and assemble the 
third bucket, push the buckets gradually paying attention to the seal pins.
Rotate the lock twist such that it secure the bucket from moving axial, 
then punch the lock twist with the two diametrically opposite peen marks with 
around nosed punch.
First Stage Bucket Re-assembly
Arrange the bucket in accordance to the balance sheet.
Place the lock twist pins in their slots. (Anti seize compound 
 is recommended to use for pines)
Assemble buckets with their radial & axial seal pins.
Rotate the lock twist such that it secures the bucket from 
 axial movement.
Punch the lock twist heads with around nosed punch to lock it 
 in the rotor slots with two diametrically opposite peen marks.
Exhaust Hood Re-assembly
Lower the upper half of the exhaust hood and tight the horizontal joint bolts 
 of inner and outer flanges be sure that new gaskets are used on the horizontal 
 joint of the inner gas path cone & the air baffle is properly located in the 
 groove of the seal of bearing NO 2 before lowering the hood.
Assemble the horizontal joint bolting 
 insulation shield.
Assemble the exhaust turning vanes (diffuser) 
 ensure the position of gas seal plates between the diffuser & stack.
First & Second Nozzle 
Re-assembly
Clean thoroughly the turbine shell and 
 discharge casing
Coat the seal-second stage nozzle spring seal 
 with anti seize
Roll in the second-stage nozzle when in 
 position and supported on the lifting rig insert and bolt the support shims
Lower the second stage nozzle lower half onto 
 the supporting lugs and inserts the bottom eccentric pin.
Assemble the two lower axial holding pins at 
 45.
Assemble the lower half inter stage packing 
 (labyrinth) and spring adjusts the clearances as recommended by the 
 manufacture drawing.
Roll in the lower half of the first stage 
 nozzle and while the nozzle is still supported on the lifting hoist insert the 
 horizontal supporting lugs and bolt tightly and then lower the nozzle.
Assemble the first stage nozzle bottom 
 eccentric pin.
Tighten the first nozzle bottom holding clamp 
 and check their clearance.
Take a complete set of turbine clearance and record the results in the attached 
 sheet
 ** Note that the clearances on the 
 packing and the second stage nozzle must be taken while the nozzle must be 
 waged against the second stage shrouds (this is its running position).
Assemble the upper half of the supporting 
 ring.
Assemble the upper half of the first stage 
 nozzle.
Assemble the upper half of second stage nozzle 
 diaphragm.
Assemble the upper half of second stage 
 nozzle.
Assemble the clamps to the first stage nozzle 
 horizontal joint and check the clearance of the lug U clamp record this 
 clearance on the attached sheet
Assemble the second nozzle clamps and record the results in the attached sheet.
Assemble the two packing strips into the outer 
 seal groove of the first stage nozzle; verify that the lap of the strips is 
 not in line to minimize the possibility of leakage.
Assemble the transition pieces. Starting from 
 the chamber No 5 and work upper wards from that point be sure that the 
 transition pieces are fully engage in the first stage nozzle before tightening 
 the center holding bolts.
Assemble the side seals (L seals) and locking 
 bolt washer combination between each transition pieces.
Shell Casing 
Re-assembly
Check thoroughly turbine shell cleaning.
Coat the mating surfaces of the turbine shell hood and discharge casing with a 
 light film of anti-seize.
Check that all is secure within the shell area before assemble, rotate the 
 turbine rotor with ratchet mechanism check if there were any abnormal sound.
Assemble the shells upper half using 4 guide rods and the two jack bolts 
 mechanism pay attention to the turbine shell level during lowering with jack 
 bolts.
Tighten the shell bolts according to the bolting sequence.
Assemble the first and second stage nozzle upper eccentric pins; second stage 
 axial holding bolts at 45 and the bore scope plugs.
Assemble the outer combustion casing using new gasket on the casings and fix 
 them in the groove with grease in two spots.
Remove all support jacks from the unit.
Remove all support jacking located under the turbine.
Combustion Component
Re-assembly
A - 
Cleaning
Clean all mating flange faces of any gasket material.
Clean all hardware bolts & nuts with wire-brush to remove traces of anti-seize 
 or rust.
Lock maintained fuel nozzle with steel lock wire.
B - Combustion Liner
Assemble liner No 5 to the chamber. Slide the crossfire tubes from chamber No 
 6 & No 4 into liner No 5
Assemble liner No 4.
Slide crossfire tube from liner No 5 into position between liners No 4 & No 5 
 and lock it with retainers.
Follow the a/m procedure for the remaining chambers.
Energize the ignition transformers and observes that the spark plugs are 
 properly.
Check the flame detector works properly by expose the scanner to suitable 
 light.
Assemble the spark plugs and the flam detector.
Fuel 
Nozzles & Aaccessoires
Pipe
Assemble the combustion covers take in consideration that the two larger bolts 
 in the flanges are to be mated with the holes in the cover and casing.
Reassemble the fuel nozzles but do not tighten bolts firmly.
Reassemble the fuel piping and when mating with the nozzle flanges. Tight the 
 nozzle bolts firmly. Check the gas lines flange for leakage with soapy 
 solution.
Re-assemble the Turbine Compartment Roof 
and CO2 Fire Fighting System Pipes
Turbine / load gear alignment check
Mount the alignment fixture on the load gear flange.
Rotate the load gear shaft from the 
 generator coupling. Record the face 
 and rim reading in the sheet (attachment # 6) The alignment reading should be 
 within following Tolerance.
Take in consideration the face reading referenced to 12 flange diameter and 
 correction should be made if the face reading has been taken at less 
 diameter.
Repeat the alignment reading at moderate temperature (preferable after 
 midnight)
Re-assemble the load coupling and torque the bolts in 
 sequence as described in sheet (attachment # 7).
Re-assemble the load coupling guard and its 
 drainpipe
Re-assemble the generator coupling cover.
Turbine 
 / accessory gear alignment check
Mount the alignment fixture on the accessory gear flange.
Rotate the accessory gear shaft and record the face and rim reading in sheet 
 (attachment # 6), which should be within the following tolerances:
Take in consideration the face reading 
 referenced to 12 flange diameter and correction should be made if the face 
 reading has been taken at less diameter.
Re-assemble the accessory coupling and torque the bolts in sequence as described 
 in sheet (attachment # 7).
Re-assemble the coupling guard.
Check generator the unit component.
Perform the cranking checks on the turbine.
Preparation the unit for 
start after inspection
Revise & check the clearness & cleanness of working site.
Check the availability of DC & AC power supplies.
Check batteries voltage should not be less than 105 V.
Check the lube oil level and the fuel oil tank of starting diesel engine.
Check the level of main tank lube oil in normal level.
Operate the emergency lube oil pump check direction of rotation and the 
discharge Pressure.
Check lube oil flow through sight glass at bearing NO. (1, 2, 3).
Check the level of cooling water tanks.
Check valves position of fuel supply system in operation position.
Check the position of cooling air dampers.
Check readiness of unit (No trip signal is initiated) and the ready light signal 
is on.

Check the availability of DC & AC power supplies.
Check batteries voltage should not be less than 105 V.

Check the position of cooling air dampers.

is on.
Operation checks
Operate the unit at different speeds (200 
 r.p.m, crank speed, fire position, full speed no load)
check the unit for:
 a. Leakage of fuel gas line (test with soapy 
 solution).
 b. Leakage of cooling and seal air pipes.
 c. Abnormal noise or excessive vibration.
Operate the unit at (different loads 0%, 25%,
